 Navigating the FAFSA: A Parent’s Guide to Unlocking College Affordability at the College of Charleston 
 November 17, 2026 
 Madeline Jacaruso 
 Main Feature 
 Everything you need to know about the FAFSA and applying for financial aid at the College of Charleston! 
 Listen to this article 
 Image generated with Microsoft Copilot 
 Planning for your child’s college involves looking carefully at a few important things:
 finding the right academic fit
 checking out the campus culture
 figuring out the cost
 To make a College of Charleston education as affordable as possible, the most important first step is filling out the FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) .
 Many families make the mistake of thinking their household income is too high to get any help. But financial experts encourage every family to fill out the FAFSA. Not only does it open the door to over $150 billion in federal aid – like grants, work-study programs and student loans – but states and colleges, including the College of Charleston, use the FAFSA to hand out their own need-based scholarships and grants.
 Step-by-Step: Applying for financial aid at the College of Charleston 
 Key FAFSA Deadlines and Timeline
 Timing is everything when it comes to getting the most financial aid for college!
 When it opens: The FAFSA usually opens on or about Oct. 1 every year for the next school year. Try to submit it as early as you can.
 College of Charleston priority deadline (Feb. 1): Students who finish and file by this date get first-in-line consideration for federal, state and school aid. If you wait until after this date, some grants and school money might have run out.
 Time investment: For most families, filling out the FAFSA takes less than an hour. Allowing your tax information to be transferred directly from the IRS cuts this time down even more!
 Checklist: What Information Do You Need?
 Getting ready ahead of time is the best way to make filling out the FAFSA stress-free. Since most students need their parents or guardians to help with money details, it helps to gather the following items early:
 Studentaid.gov account: Both the student and at least one parent (or helper) needs their own verified studentaid.gov account . This works like a secure online signature.
 Social Security Numbers: You will need these for both the student and the parent(s) helping out.
 Note: Gather recent federal income tax returns, W-2 forms and records of any untaxed money, cash, savings and investments only if the student/parent/guardian either (a) worked but was not required to file taxes OR (b) has not yet filed taxes for the year in question. 
 Who Needs to Help?
 Depending on your family situation, more than one person might need to pitch in and fill out a part of the form:
 Parents: needed for dependent students
 Stepparents: needed if the main supporting parent has remarried
 Spouses: needed for students who are married
 What Happens After You Submit the FAFSA?
 Once your FAFSA has been successfully sent and processed, your information is securely shared with the colleges you listed on the application.
 The College of Charleston will use this information to figure out what kind of financial aid you qualify for and to build a personalized money package just for you.
 Ready to start applying for financial aid at the College of Charleston? 
 We Are Here to Help
 Figuring out financial aid can feel like a lot to handle, but you don’t have to do it by yourself. If you have questions about the FAFSA, deadlines or your student’s financial aid, the College of Charleston Office of Financial Assistance and Veterans Affairs is ready to help your family every step of the way!
